facts.statement: Gargantuavis is an extinct genus of large, primitive birds that contains only one species, Gargantuavis philoinos.
facts.quote: Gargantuavis (meaning 'gargantuan bird') is an extinct genus of large, primitive bird containing the single species Gargantuavis philoinos.

facts.statement: Fossils of Gargantuavis date to 73.5 and 71.5 million years ago and have been found in northern Spain, southern France, and Romania.
facts.quote: Its fossils were discovered in several formations dating to 73.5 and 71.5 million years ago in what is now northern Spain, Southern France, and Romania.

facts.statement: Gargantuavis is the largest known bird from the Mesozoic era, weighing approximately 141 kg and standing between the size of a cassowary and an ostrich.
facts.quote: Gargantuavis is the largest known bird of the Mesozoic, a size ranging between the cassowary and the ostrich, and a mass of 141 kg like modern ostriches

facts.statement: The first fossil of Gargantuavis was discovered in 1995 in the Var department of southeastern France.
facts.quote: The first Gargantuavis fossil was found in 1995 in Var, southeastern France.

facts.statement: The genus name Gargantuavis honors Gargantua, the giant protagonist of Francois Rabelais's 16th-century novel, combined with the Latin word for bird.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to Gargantua, the giant and protagonist of the 16th-century French novel The Life of Gargantua and of Pantagruel by Francois Rabelais, and the Latin avis.

facts.statement: Research suggests Gargantuavis possesses primitive features, challenging earlier views that it was closely related to modern birds.
facts.quote: It was once thought to be closely related to modern birds, but the 2019 discovery of a pelvis identified as cf. Elopteryx nopcsai from what was Hațeg Island (present-day Romania) shows several primitive features.

facts.statement: Analysis of its femur indicates Gargantuavis was a graviportal animal adapted for supporting weight rather than for running.
facts.quote: Its femur shows that it was a graviportal form rather than cursorial, not adapted for running.

facts.statement: The shape of Gargantuavis's head is unknown because no cranial remains have been discovered.
facts.quote: No cranial remains have been found, so the shape of the head is unknown.

facts.statement: The single known cervical vertebra suggests Gargantuavis had a long, slender neck that likely precluded a massive skull.
facts.quote: However, the only known cervical vertebra suggests that Gargantuavis had a rather long and slender neck, which seems to preclude the presence of a massive skull.

facts.statement: The broad structure of Gargantuavis's pelvis indicates it was not capable of fast running.
facts.quote: The rather broad pelvis shows that Gargantuavis was not a fast runner.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that Gargantuavis may have lived in environments far from rivers and floodplains, which would explain the rarity of its fossils.
facts.quote: It is possible that Gargantuavis lived mainly in an environment that was not compatible with fossilization, such as areas far from the rivers and floodplains, which represent most of the fossiliferous deposits in the late Campanian-early Maastrichtian of France and Spain.

facts.statement: The ecological role of Gargantuavis is debated because it coexisted with large predators like abelisaurid and dromaeosaurid theropods, unlike giant Cenozoic birds.
facts.quote: Contrary to the giant terrestrial Cenozoic birds that lived in ecosystems without predators (or including only small carnivores), Gargantuavis cohabited with abelisaurid and dromaeosaurid theropods, so the place of this giant terrestrial bird in the Late Cretaceous ecosystems of the Ibero-Armorican island is unclear.

facts.statement: Gargantuavis is the sole member of the monotypic family Gargantuaviidae.
facts.quote: It is the only member of the monotypic family Gargantuaviidae.

facts.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, the regions where Gargantuavis fossils are found were part of the Ibero-Armorican island in the Tethys Sea.
facts.quote: During the Late Cretaceous, Europe was an archipelago. Southern France and north-western Spain where its fossils are found was part of the large Ibero-Armorican island in the prehistoric Tethys Sea.

facts.statement: Gargantuavis was initially thought to be related to Patagopteryx, but later studies placed it in the monotypic family Gargantuaviidae within Ornithurae, making it more closely related to modern birds.
facts.quote: It was once thought to be closely related to the archaic Patagopteryx, but a study of the complete femur suggested that the species belongs to Ornithuromorpha, and probably Ornithurae, being more closely related to moderns birds than to, belonging to its own monotypic family Gargantuaviidae.

facts.statement: Gargantuavis is classified in the family Gargantuaviidae.
facts.quote: familia: †Gargantuaviidae

facts.statement: The genus Gargantuavis was named by Buffetaut and Le Loeuff in 1998.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Buffetaut & Le Loeuff, 1998

facts.statement: Gargantuavis lived from the late Campanian to the early Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Campaniense tardío - Maastrichtiense temprano

facts.statement: The first fossils of Gargantuavis were found in the Marnes Rouges Inferieures formation, dated to approximately 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Sus primeros fósiles fueron descubiertos en la Formación Marnes Rouges Inferieures, la cual ha sido datada en aproximadamente 71 millones de años de antigüedad.

facts.statement: Gargantuavis was a large, flightless bird that occupied an ecological niche similar to modern ratites or primitive theropods.
facts.quote: Gargantuavis no volaba, ocupando un nicho ecológico semejante al de las actuales aves ratites o los terópodos más primitivos.

facts.statement: The first fossil of Gargantuavis was discovered in 1995 in Var, France.
facts.quote: El primer fósil de Gargantuavis fue hallado en 1995 en Var, Francia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Gargantuavis are known from six European localities, mostly in southern France.
facts.quote: En total se conocen especímenes de Gargantuavis de seis localidades europeas, la mayoría siendo del sur de Francia:

facts.statement: A partial sacrum found in a quarry near Laño, Spain, described in 2017, was the first specimen of Gargantuavis known outside of France.
facts.quote: En una cantera cerca del pueblo español de Laño (Condado de Treviño), se encontró otro sinsacro parcial (MCNA 2538) descrito en 2017, siendo el primer espécimen conocido por fuera de Francia.

facts.statement: A pelvis was found in 2019 in the Sânpetru Formation of Romania, on the former Hațeg Island.
facts.quote: Finalmente, de la Formación Sânpetru de Rumania, en la antigua Isla de Hațeg se encontró una pelvis en 2019.

facts.statement: Knowledge of Gargantuavis comes from limited skeletal parts including the synsacrum, ilia, and at least one partial femur that fits the pelvis.
facts.quote: Lo que se sabe de Gargantuavis proviene de varios especímenes que representan unas cuantas partes limitadas del esqueleto: el sinsacro (las vértebras fusionadas sobre la cadera), los iliones (huesos de la cadera), y al menos un fémur parcial (el hueso del muslo), el cual fue referido a esta especie basándose en el hecho de que parece encajar bien con la cadera.

facts.statement: Besides its large size, the most unusual feature of Gargantuavis was its pelvis.
facts.quote: Aparte de su gran tamaño, el rasgo más inusual de Gargantuavis era su pelvis.

facts.statement: Although wide, the hip proportions of Gargantuavis were more similar to most birds than initially thought.
facts.quote: Las caderas de Gargantuavis, aunque eran anchas, tenían proporciones más similares a las de la mayoría de las aves de lo que se pensó inicialmente.

facts.statement: Because no cranial material of Gargantuavis is known, its diet remains undetermined.
facts.quote: Ya que no se conoce material craneal de Gargantuavis, su dieta permanece indeterminada.

facts.statement: Unlike many Cenozoic giant land birds that evolved without large predators, Gargantuavis coexisted with abelisaurids and dromaeosaurids, creating mystery about its habits and role.
facts.quote: Al contrario que con gran parte de las gigantescas aves terrestres del Cenozoico que evolucionaron en ausencia de grandes depredadores, Gargantuavis cohabitaba con abelisaurios y dromeosáuridos, creando un mayor misterio sobre los hábitos y roles de la criatura.

facts.statement: Histology shows Gargantuavis grew rapidly before slowing down for at least 10 years before reaching sexual maturity, a pattern seen in extinct moas and kiwis.
facts.quote: La histología de los materiales conocidos muestran que Gargantuavis crecía rápidamente hasta llegar un periodo de crecimiento ralentizado, de al menos 10 años antes de alcanzar la madurez sexual; un patrón parecido se conoce en las moas extintas y el kiwi, otras aves de islas.

facts.statement: Gargantuavis likely inhabited environments unfavorable for fossilization, such as rivers and alluvial plains, which make up most fossil sites on the island.
facts.quote: Es probable que habitase ambientes poco propicios para la fosilización, como ríos y llanuras aluviales, que representan la mayoría de yacimientos fósiles de la isla.

facts.statement: Sediment analysis indicates Gargantuavis lived in a semi-arid environment with high seasonal climate variation.
facts.quote: Análisis de los sedimentos indican que se trataba de un ambiente semiárido y un clima con gran variación estacional.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggested Gargantuavis was a giant pterosaur rather than a bird, but this hypothesis was rejected due to bird-like features.
facts.quote: Some researchers suggested that Gargantuavis was not a stem-bird at all, but rather a giant pterosaur, but this was rejected based on the presence of more bird-like conditions.

facts.statement: Other authors questioned the classification of Gargantuavis, claiming it was a basal ornithurine similar to Hesperornithies, while the original study authors maintained their cautious conclusion.
facts.quote: This was questioned by other authors, and it is claimed that it was a basal ornithurine, at an evolutionary level similar to that of Hesperornithies, but the authors of the original study stood by their 'cautious' conclusion.

facts.statement: Analysis of the femur identified Gargantuavis as a member of Ornithuromorpha, a lineage related to modern birds, and the sole member of the family Gargantuaviidae.
facts.quote: con el análisis del fémur posicionó a Gargantuavis como miembro de Ornithuromorpha, como un pariente de las aves modernas y miembro único de la familia Gargantuaviidae.

facts.statement: The shape of its femur suggests Gargantuavis was not a giant member of the Enantiornithes, an archaic group of birds.
facts.quote: La forma de su fémur sugiere que Gargantuavis no se trataba de un miembro gigantesco de los enantiornitas, un grupo de aves arcaicas

facts.statement: Features of the pelvis found on the island of Hațeg, including a supratrochanteric process on the femur and unfused pelvic bones, indicate Gargantuavis was not closely related to Ornithurae.
facts.quote: La pelvis descubierta en lo que fue la isla de Hațeg muestra un proceso supratrocántico en el fémur, la ausencia de un cuerpo de glucógeno y la falta de fusión de los huesos pélvicos respecto a la cavidad de la cadera indican que no estaba relacionado estrechamente con Ornithurae

facts.statement: Researchers initially thought Gargantuavis might be closely related to Patagopteryx, but femur analysis later placed it in Ornithuromorpha.
facts.quote: Durante esta primera época se pensó que podría ser un pariente cercano de Patagopteryx, pero con el análisis del fémur posicionó a Gargantuavis como miembro de Ornithuromorpha

facts.statement: The systematic position of Gargantuavis relative to other birds remains uncertain due to the fragmentary nature of the fossils.
facts.quote: La posición sistemática de Gargantuavis respecto al resto de aves es incierta por la naturaleza fragmentaria de los fósiles.

facts.statement: The femur shape and derived traits like sacral vertebrae count and a saddle-shaped cervical vertebra suggest Gargantuavis belonged to a more derived lineage rather than the Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: La forma de su fémur sugiere que Gargantuavis no se trataba de un miembro gigantesco de los enantiornitas, un grupo de aves arcaicas; sino que pertenecía a un linaje más derivado, también apoyado por la cantidad de vértebras presentes en el sinsacro y la más avanzada condición heterocélica (con articulación en forma de silla de montar) de la única vértebra cervical conocida.

facts.statement: Contemporary avian theropods from Hațeg, Elopteryx and Balaur, show some relationship with Gargantuavis, suggesting a native Cretaceous European archipelago clado, though their affinities remain ambiguous.
facts.quote: Los terópodos avianos contemporáneos de Hațeg, Elopteryx y Balaur presentan algún parentesco con Gargantuavis, lo que puede indicar la existencia de un clado de animales nativos al archipiélago europeo del Cretácico Superior, aunque sus afinidades son algo ambiguas.

facts.statement: Gargantuavis lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 2009, researchers proposed Gargantuavis might have been a giant pterosaur, but studying bone shape and internal structure confirmed its identity as an avialan.
facts.quote: En 2009 un grupo de investigadores sugirió que se pudo haber tratado de un pterosaurio gigantesco, cuando esta idea fue puesta a prueba al estudiar la forma y la estructura interna de los huesos, su identidad como avialano prevaleció.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Gargantuavis belongs to Ornithothoraces, the group including modern birds and their closest ancestors, due to fragmentary fossil evidence.
facts.quote: La posición sistemática de Gargantuavis respecto al resto de aves es incierta por la naturaleza fragmentaria de los fósiles.
